A Growth customer paying $149/month with a single 3-hour outage in a 30-day month has monthly uptime of approximately 99.58%, which falls below the Growth commitment of 99.9% but is at least 99.0%, so they are eligible for a 10% credit. [Doc: northwind_sla_support_tiers, Section: 3. Service credits]
The credit amount is 10% of $149, which equals $14.90, applied to a future invoice rather than paid out in cash. [Doc: northwind_sla_support_tiers, Section: 3. Service credits]
To claim the credit, the customer must open a support ticket within 30 days after the end of the month in which the downtime occurred, referencing the dates and times affected; approved credits are applied to the next invoice. [Doc: northwind_sla_support_tiers, Section: 4. Claiming a credit]

On the Starter plan, uploads are limited to 10 MB, so a 30 MB file exceeds the limit and causes a 413 payload_too_large error. [Doc: northwind_troubleshooting_faq, Section: 4. I get 413 payload_too_large]
The recommended options are to compress the file, split it into smaller parts, or upgrade to a plan with a higher limit (50 MB on Growth or 200 MB on Enterprise). [Doc: northwind_troubleshooting_faq, Section: 4. I get 413 payload_too_large]

A 4-hour Sev2 first-response target for Growth customers is available only as part of the Premier Support add-on, not as part of the base Growth plan. [Doc: northwind_sla_support_tiers, Section: 12. Premier Support add-on] [Doc: northwind_sla_support_tiers, Section: 9. First-response targets]

Only users with the Owner role can cancel a plan by going to Settings > Billing > Cancel plan. [Doc: northwind_refund_cancellation_policy, Section: 8. Cancelling a plan]
Paid features stay active until the end of the paid period, after which the account reverts to the Free plan. [Doc: northwind_refund_cancellation_policy, Section: 8. Cancelling a plan]
Projects exceeding Free plan limits become read-only for 30 days and are then permanently deleted, so data should be exported before then. [Doc: northwind_refund_cancellation_policy, Section: 8. Cancelling a plan]

Every webhook delivery includes the header X-Northwind-Signature: t=<timestamp>,v1=<signature>. [Doc: northwind_api_reference, Section: 9. Webhooks]
The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 of the string <timestamp>.<raw request body> using your endpoint secret. [Doc: northwind_api_reference, Section: 9. Webhooks]
Verify the signature using the raw request body, not re-serialized. [Doc: northwind_troubleshooting_faq, Section: 7. My webhooks are not arriving]
Reject deliveries whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes old. [Doc: northwind_api_reference, Section: 9. Webhooks] [Doc: northwind_onboarding_guide, Section: 9. Production readiness checklist]

Change the base path from /v2 to /v3. [Doc: northwind_onboarding_guide, Section: 10. Migrating from API v2]
API v2 was shut down on 2026-03-31 and requests to v2 endpoints now return 410 Gone. [Doc: northwind_api_reference, Section: 11. Versioning and deprecation] [Doc: northwind_platform_policy_changelog, Section: 5. 2026-03-31 — API v2 shut down]
